subject: history
title: Postwar Britain Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the Windrush generation, Ugandan Asians and EU migrants.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Windrush, Ugandan Asians and EU enlargement.
final_note: You learned how migration reshaped Britain after 1948.

concepts.def: Ship arrived Tilbury 22 June 1948 with 492 Caribbean migrants
Idi Amin expelled 27,000 to Britain in 1972

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 22 June 1948 HMT Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury with 492 Caribbean passengers.

The 1948 British Nationality Act gave them UK citizenship. They filled gaps on London Transport, the new NHS and in factories. By 1971 about 500,000 Caribbean and South Asian migrants had settled.

The 1958 Notting Hill riots saw white youths attacking Caribbean homes.

The 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act restricted entry. The 1965 and 1976 Race Relations Acts outlawed discrimination. Enoch Powell's 1968 'Rivers of Blood' speech inflamed racism.

In 1972 Uganda's Idi Amin expelled the Asian community — about 27,000 came to Britain.

From 2004, EU enlargement let Poles, Czechs and others work freely; about 1 million Eastern Europeans came by 2010. Brexit (2016) ended free movement after 2020.
